sub_tasks.requirements: The TTFT-aware prefill reordering policy (Algorithm 2) with lookahead window w, TTFT-satisfying task counting (Eqs. 3-4), and starvation prevention via postponement counters has been implemented on each prefill queue.
The core Algorithm 2 reordering routine is implemented and integrated into each prefill worker's queue scheduling.

Code has been implemented that maintains a prefill queue Q per prefill worker (and per decode worker for local execution) whose head elements can be peeked, reordered, and dequeued for reordering decisions.

verification.spec: Import the worker module and verify that both PrefillWorker and DecodeWorker classes expose a prefill_queue attribute supporting peek(n), reorder(order), and dequeue() operations. Instantiate a queue, enqueue 5 mock tasks, and confirm peek(3) returns first 3, reorder([2,0,1]) reorders them, and dequeue() returns the new head.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that peeks up to w head elements from the prefill queue to form the lookahead window W = {r_1, r_2, ...} before each scheduling decision (Algorithm 2 line 1).

verification.spec: Invoke the reordering scheduler with a queue containing 10 mock tasks and w=3. Verify via logging/instrumentation that Q.peek(3) is called and exactly 3 tasks form the candidate window W. Repeat with w=5 and queue size 2, verify window contains 2 tasks (min(w, queue_len)).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enumerates all feasible orderings π over the window W in Algorithm 2 (with pruning via postponement capacity check on line 3).

verification.spec: Instrument the reordering routine to log every candidate ordering evaluated. With a window of w=3 tasks and all postponement counters at 0, verify all 3!=6 permutations are enumerated. With one task's counter at w, verify orderings postponing it further are skipped (line 3-4 pruning).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, after selecting the optimal ordering π*, calls Q.reorder(π*) on the queue head and dequeues the first element for execution (Algorithm 2 lines 8-9).

verification.spec: Mock Q.reorder and Q.dequeue. Trigger a scheduling round with 3 tasks and a known optimal ordering pi*. Assert Q.reorder is called exactly once with pi* and Q.dequeue is called exactly once immediately after, returning the head task under pi*.

sub_tasks.requirements: The default lookahead window size w is configurable and set to w = 3 by default, as stated in the experimental protocols.

verification.spec: Load the default AMPD config and assert that the lookahead window size hyperparameter w equals 3. Verify it can be overridden by passing --window-size or via config file, and the new value propagates to the reordering scheduler.

sub_tasks.requirements: TTFT-satisfying task counting via Equations (3) and (4) is implemented to score candidate orderings.

Code has been implemented that computes the predicted completion time of the π(k)-th task (relative to T_now) as the cumulative sum of estimated prefill times t_pre(r) of the first k tasks under ordering π, per Equation (3).

verification.spec: Construct a window of 4 mock tasks with prescribed t_pre values [100,200,150,50] ms. For ordering pi=[2,0,3,1] compute expected completion times as cumulative sums (150, 250, 300, 500). Call the completion-time helper and assert it returns exactly these values for k=1..4.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that estimates each task's prefill time cost t_pre(r) via the performance model function T_pre(l_hist, l_incr; θ) using the task's history length and incremental input length.

verification.spec: Create a task with l_hist=1024, l_incr=256 under a known parallelism strategy theta. Call the prefill-time estimator and verify it invokes the profiler's T_pre(l_hist, l_incr; theta) function with these exact arguments and returns the profiler's result.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes S_π, the count of tasks in W whose predicted completion time plus (T_now - T_enq(r)) does not exceed the TTFT SLO threshold, per Equation (4).

verification.spec: With window of 3 tasks having known T_enq, mock T_now, and known t_pre values, hand-compute S_pi for a specific ordering using Eq(4): S_pi = |{k : (T_now - T_enq(pi(k))) + sum_{j<=k} t_pre(pi(j)) <= TTFT_thres}|. Call the implementation and assert equality with hand-computed value across 3 test cases.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that selects the ordering π* = argmax_π S_π that maximizes the number of TTFT-satisfying tasks within the window W (Algorithm 2 lines 5-6).

verification.spec: Construct a window where one specific ordering yields the unique maximum S_pi (e.g., FIFO gives S=1 but reversing gives S=3). Call the reorder selector and assert the returned pi* equals the analytically maximum-S ordering. Also verify tie-breaking is deterministic.

sub_tasks.requirements: The TTFT SLO threshold used in Equation (4) is retrieved from the per-model, per-trace SLO configuration (e.g., 2500ms for Llama-3.1-70B HotpotQA) rather than being hard-coded.

verification.spec: Configure AMPD with TTFT_thres=2500ms for Llama-3.1-70B HotpotQA. Instrument S_pi computation to log the TTFT threshold value used. Run one scheduling round and verify the logged value is 2500ms, not a hard-coded constant. Repeat for GAIA (1500ms) and confirm value changes accordingly.

sub_tasks.requirements: Starvation prevention via per-task postponement counters is implemented so no task is postponed more than w times.
Code has been implemented that maintains an integer postponement counter attached to each queued prefill task, initialized to zero at enqueue time.

verification.spec: Enqueue 5 mock tasks into a prefill queue. Immediately inspect each task's postponement_counter attribute and assert all equal 0. Verify the attribute is an integer type.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, after selecting π*, increments the postponement counter for every task in W whose position under π* is later than its original position in the queue (Algorithm 2 line 7).

verification.spec: Create window W = [A, B, C] with all counters at 0. Force pi* = [B, A, C] (A moves from index 0 to 1; C stays). Trigger reordering and assert A.postponement_counter == 1, B.counter == 0, C.counter == 0 after the round.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that skips (does not consider) any candidate ordering π which would further postpone a task whose postponement counter has already reached w (Algorithm 2 lines 3-4).

verification.spec: Set w=3. Create window [A, B, C] with A.postponement_counter=3 (== w). Instrument the ordering enumeration to log all considered orderings. Assert every considered ordering places A at index 0 (i.e., A is never postponed further). Orderings like [B, A, C] must be skipped.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that when a task's postponement counter equals w, only orderings preserving that task's position (or moving it earlier) are considered, ensuring the task is eventually scheduled within a bounded number of reordering rounds.

verification.spec: Unit test: enqueue task T at head of a queue with w=3 other tasks each having tight TTFT so pi* would repeatedly postpone T. Run scheduling rounds and verify: (a) T's counter increments each time it is postponed, (b) once counter reaches w=3, next round schedules T (dequeues it), demonstrating starvation prevention.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral correctness of the reordering policy is verified via unit tests.
A unit test with a hand-crafted window of tasks (with known t_pre and T_enq values) verifies that the reordering selects an ordering whose S_π value matches the analytically computed maximum.

verification.spec: Unit test with hand-crafted window: 3 tasks with t_pre=[100,50,200] and T_enq offsets making TTFT_thres=300ms. Enumerate all 6 orderings analytically, compute S_pi for each, identify max. Call scheduler and assert selected pi* achieves the same max S_pi value.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that with w=1 the reordering policy degenerates to FIFO (no reordering), and that with w>=2 shorter TTFT-tight tasks are moved ahead of longer slack tasks when it increases S_π.

verification.spec: Test 1: with w=1, verify only FIFO ordering is considered and the head element is always dequeued unchanged across 5 scheduling rounds. Test 2: with w=3 and a window where the 3rd task has very tight TTFT slack (would be missed under FIFO), verify pi* moves it ahead of longer-slack tasks and its predicted completion satisfies TTFT.

sub_tasks.requirements: Empirical results confirm the prefill reordering policy improves SLO attainment as reported in the paper.
In the ablation study on Llama-3.1-70B at 2 req/s, enabling prefill reordering on top of adaptive routing further improves SLO attainment by 13.42%-14.81% over the AR-only variant, matching Figure 5.

verification.spec: Run three configurations on Llama-3.1-70B at 2 req/s on DuReader and GAIA traces: (a) no AR+PR (baseline), (b) AR only, (c) AMPD (AR+PR). Compute SLO attainment. Verify that (c) - (b) improvement is within [13.42%, 14.81%] on both traces.

sub_tasks.requirements: In the sensitivity study on Llama-3.1-70B DuReader at 2 req/s, SLO attainment across window sizes w ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5} varies by less than 3 percentage points, matching Figure 6 (left).

verification.spec: Run AMPD on Llama-3.1-70B DuReader at 2 req/s for w ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5} (holding alpha=0.9, beta=0.85 fixed). Record SLO attainment for each. Compute max - min across the four values; verify it is < 3 percentage points.

Send a single test request and confirm KV cache is transferred from prefill to decode over NIXL/RDMA (visible in Dynamo logs or NIXL counters).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that in the Dynamo baseline all prefill tasks (both initial and incremental) are routed to prefill workers only, with no local execution on decode workers and no AMPD-specific adaptive routing or reordering enabled.

verification.spec: Run Dynamo baseline with a multi-round trace (e.g., HotpotQA) at 1 req/s. Log the location where each prefill task (initial and incremental) executes. Assert 100% of prefill tasks execute on prefill workers, 0% on decode workers, and that AMPD's adaptive-routing and reordering code paths are disabled (feature flags off).

Verify the client requires no code changes (only endpoint URL swap) and both systems accept the identical request payloads and return responses in the same schema.

sub_tasks.requirements: The vLLM baseline has been set up as a PD-colocated LLM serving system, using the same models and traces as AMPD.

verification.spec: Verify a script/module exists that launches a vLLM server (e.g., `python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server` or equivalent) with prefill and decode co-located on the same GPUs and continuous batching enabled (default vLLM behavior). sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the vLLM baseline uses its standard scheduling policy in which prefill tasks are prioritized over decoding, matching the vLLM behavior referenced in the paper.

Inspect scheduler logs or trace to confirm that when a new prefill task arrives, it preempts/precedes ongoing decode batches (prefill priority). Verify by checking that TTFT of newly-arrived requests is not blocked by long decode sequences.

verification.spec: Verify a launch script exists for vLLM-Continuum baseline that enables the KV cache TTL mechanism and session-aware prioritization referenced in Li et al. 2025. Confirm the code imports/invokes the Continuum-modified vLLM (not vanilla vLLM), and that a session-id field is honored in the request API. Submit a multi-round request and confirm the server handles it.

Confirm session A's next-round prefill is scheduled ahead of session B's initial prefill when both are queued simultaneously, demonstrating session-aware prioritization. sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the local-execution time cost estimator on decode worker d computes t_local = T_pre(l_hist, l_incr; theta_d) + sum over queued tasks of their T_pre estimates (queuing time), matching Equation (1) in the paper.

verification.spec: Instantiate the local cost estimator with a synthetic performance model T_pre that returns known values; enqueue a synthetic prefill queue; assert the returned t_local equals T_pre(l_hist, l_incr; theta_d) + sum of T_pre over queued tasks within a small numerical tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the remote-execution time cost estimator on prefill worker i computes t_remote_i = T_pre(l_hist, l_incr; theta_p_i) + T_kv (round-trip transmission) + queuing time on prefill worker i, matching Equation (2).

verification.spec: Instantiate the remote cost estimator with synthetic T_pre, T_kv, and a synthetic prefill queue; assert the returned t_remote_i equals the sum of the three components (compute, KV round-trip, queuing) within a small numerical tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that, given an ordering pi over the lookahead window W, the predicted completion time (relative to T_now) of the k-th task in pi equals sum_{j=1..k} t_pre(pi(j)) + (T_now - T_enq(pi(k))), matching Equation (3).

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic window of 3-4 tasks with known enqueue times and t_pre values; call the completion-time predictor for a specified ordering; assert per-position outputs equal the closed-form value from Eq. (3).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the number of TTFT-satisfying tasks S_pi within window W under ordering pi equals the count of indices k for which the predicted completion time is <= TTFT_thres, matching Equation (4), and the reordering policy selects pi* = argmax_pi S_pi.

verification.spec: Given a synthetic window and TTFT threshold, enumerate all permutations and assert the implementation's S_pi values match the reference count from Eq. (4); assert the chosen pi* maximizes S_pi.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the offline planner minimizes an auxiliary variable Z (worst-case P95 latency) subject to the C1/C2/C3 constraints of the ILP formulation in Equation (5).

verification.spec: Construct a small synthetic instance with known tau_pre(n), tau_dec(n) coefficients, N GPUs, and T={1,2,4,8}; call the planner; assert the returned (x, y) minimizes Z subject to Z >= tau_pre(n) for any x^(n)>0, Z >= tau_dec(n) for any y^(n)>0, and sum n*(x^(n)+y^(n)) <= N, by comparing against a brute-force enumeration.

verification.spec: Inspect the planner's constraint set; assert that a constraint equivalent to sum n*(x^(n)+y^(n)) <= N is present. Additionally, feed a synthetic case where the unconstrained optimum would exceed N and assert the solver returns a solution satisfying the capacity bound.
